rounds.text: Anupam Finserv Ltd displays striking fundamental momentum, highlighted by a staggering 141% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a net profit surge of 1450% year-on-year [E21, E56]. This operational acceleration is supported by robust multi-year sales compounding, including 28% over 3 years and 45% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E17]. Valuation multiples remain highly attractive relative to peers, with the stock trading at a P/E of 18.5x and an EV/EBITDA of 13.92x, both sitting below their respective sector benchmarks of 25.26x and 21.55x [E1, E6, E11]. Furthermore, insiders are backing this growth trajectory aggressively, with promoter shareholding jumping by 22.44 percentage points from 29.31% in September 2023 to 51.75% in June 2023 [E35]. The broader macro environment provides a supportive tailwind, as the Financial Services sector registers a tailwind score of 0.83 with sector median profit growth at 20.3% [E66, E67]. Conceded: [E30], [E43], [E47], [E53].

Despite reported profit growth, Anupam Finserv Ltd suffers from severe cash flow generation issues, evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -3.63 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -3.26 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32]. This results in a dismal cash conversion ratio of -1.86x against reported profit, meaning operating cash flow represents -93% of operating profit [E30, E33]. The business exhibits consistently low profitability, reflected in a 10-year median return on equity of just 7% and a low 3-year average ROE of 5.64% [E26, E54], alongside a total absence of shareholder cash returns through a 0.00% dividend yield [E4]. Market sentiment and price action are profoundly weak, with the stock trading near its 52-week low [E5, E41], sitting 41.3% below its 52-week high [E42], and residing below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43]. Furthermore, the stock displays heavy downside risks through an annualized volatility of 56.6% [E47], a lagging relative-strength rating of 7 against the Nifty 500 [E44], and a disastrous historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -96.3% [E46], leading to a low rules-based screen score of 40 out of 100 indicating a SELL rating [E55]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing twelve-month sales growth of 45% [E17] and profit growth of 141% [E21], supported by an increasing promoter holding of 51.75% [E35] and a favorable sector tailwind in Financial Services [E66].

While operating cash flow was negative at Rs -3.63 Cr for March 2026 [E31], this must be weighed against accelerating fundamentals, including a massive 141% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and 45% sales growth [E17, E21]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], and median return on equity is low at 7% over 10 years [E26]. However, dismissing the stock for its weak price action and position near its 52-week low [E5, E41] ignores that the company is starting to outperform expectations as profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 160% [E50]. Furthermore, insiders are heavily backing this turnaround, with promoter holding surging by 22.44 percentage points to reach 51.75% [E35]. The weak moving averages and lagging relative-strength rating of 7 [E43, E44] represent backward-looking sentiment that overlooks an intrinsic value of Rs 2 per share offering a margin of safety [E38, E39], operating within a supportive Financial Services sector tailwind [E66].
